name: Peter Abelard

died.place: Priory of Saint-Marcel, near Chalon-sur-Saône, Burgundy
died.cause: Illness, while traveling to Rome to appeal his condemnation

summary: The most famous teacher of 12th-century Paris, whose logical method shaped scholastic theology, whose affair with Héloïse ended in his castration, and whose teaching was twice condemned.

key_dates.label: Master of the cathedral school of Notre-Dame, Paris
Affair with his student Héloïse; their son Astrolabe is born and they marry secretly
Castrated by men hired by Héloïse's uncle Fulbert; becomes a monk at Saint-Denis
Council of Soissons condemns his book on the Trinity; forced to burn it
Founds the oratory of the Paraclete, later given to Héloïse and her nuns
Writes the Historia Calamitatum; correspondence with Héloïse begins
Condemned at the Council of Sens and by Pope Innocent II

accomplishments.text: Drew students from across Europe to Paris and helped make it the center of learning from which the university grew.
In Sic et Non ('Yes and No') set apparently contradictory statements of the church fathers side by side with rules for reconciling them, a method that shaped scholastic theology.
Argued in logic for a middle position on universals, that general terms are meaningful words rather than real things, a key step toward 'nominalism'.
Taught in his Ethics (Know Yourself) that sin lies in consent and intention rather than in outward acts.
Taught that Christ's death saves above all by revealing God's love and awakening love in return (often called the 'moral influence' view of the atonement).
Seduced Héloïse, a gifted young woman his student and in his care in her uncle's house; he admitted in his own account that he planned the seduction.
Wrote the Historia Calamitatum, an autobiography, and exchanged letters with Héloïse that are among the most famous in literature; he also wrote hymns and a rule for her convent.

original.phrase: By doubting we come to inquiry, and by inquiry we perceive the truth.

persecution_note: Abelard suffered a violent attack and two church condemnations, the second pressed by Bernard of Clairvaux.

persecution.title: Castration by Fulbert's men
persecution.summary: Believing Abelard had abandoned Héloïse after sending her to the convent at Argenteuil, her uncle Fulbert, a canon of Notre-Dame, had men bribe Abelard's servant and castrate him in his sleep. Two of the attackers were caught and blinded and castrated in punishment.

responsible.name: Fulbert
responsible.role: Canon of Notre-Dame and Héloïse's uncle; arranged the attack

persecution.outcome: Abelard became a monk at Saint-Denis; Héloïse took the veil at Argenteuil.

persecution.title: Council of Soissons
persecution.summary: Rival teachers Alberic of Reims and Lotulf of Novara brought charges against his treatise on the Trinity. A council under the papal legate Conan of Praeneste condemned it without a proper hearing; Abelard was made to burn it with his own hands and was confined for a time in the monastery of Saint-Médard.

responsible.name: Alberic of Reims and Lotulf of Novara

persecution.outcome: Released soon after; he returned to Saint-Denis.

persecution.title: Condemnation at Sens
persecution.summary: Bernard of Clairvaux and William of Saint-Thierry drew up a list of errors from Abelard's works. At the Council of Sens Abelard refused to debate and appealed to Rome, but the bishops condemned the propositions, and Pope Innocent II confirmed the condemnation, ordered his books burned, and sentenced him to perpetual silence and confinement in a monastery.

responsible.name: William of Saint-Thierry
responsible.role: Drew up the first list of errors

defended_by.name: Peter the Venerable
defended_by.role: Abbot of Cluny; sheltered him and reconciled him with Bernard

persecution.outcome: He spent his last months at Cluny and its priory, reconciled with the church.

excommunication_note: Abelard was not formally excommunicated, but his teaching was condemned twice.

excommunications.authority: Provincial council under a papal legate
excommunications.reason: His treatise on the Trinity (Theologia 'Summi boni') condemned; he was made to burn it

excommunications.by: Council of Sens; confirmed by Pope Innocent II
excommunications.authority: Council of bishops and the papacy
excommunications.reason: Propositions from his works condemned as heretical; his books ordered burned and perpetual silence imposed
excommunications.status: Peter the Venerable obtained his reconciliation before his death and a posthumous absolution for Héloïse to keep

persecuted_others_note: No record of Peter Abelard supporting or carrying out persecution of others; he was himself condemned twice. His Dialogue of a Philosopher with a Jew and a Christian gives the Jew a sympathetic voice in describing the mistreatment Jews suffered among Christians.

sources.citation: The Letters of Abelard and Heloise, trans. Betty Radice, rev. M. T. Clanchy. London: Penguin, 2003. (Includes the Historia Calamitatum.)
M. T. Clanchy, Abelard: A Medieval Life. Oxford: Blackwell, 1997.
